label: History Painting
description: How the grand battle canvases were actually made — manner, surface and staging traditions; characteristics only, never artist names.

items.name: romanticist-battle
items.text: romanticist battle canvas, early-1800s sublime, the melee dissolving into smoke and light at its edges, small brilliant figures under an enormous violent sky, glazed atmospheric depth

items.name: baroque-melee
items.text: baroque battle-piece manner, 1600s cavalry-skirmish tradition, a churning diagonal knot of horses and pikes, tenebrist light picking single riders out of deep brown darkness

items.name: academic-salon
items.text: academic salon history painting, 1870s museum finish, life-size theatrical staging, every strap and buckle resolved, controlled even light across acres of canvas

items.name: cyclorama-panorama
items.text: battle-panorama cyclorama manner, one continuous sweeping horizon of massed action, mid-ground detail dense as tapestry, composed for a viewer turning in place

items.name: woven-tapestry
items.text: medieval battle-tapestry styling, stacked narrative registers, stylized horses caught mid-leap, wool and gilt-thread palette, margins crowded with small embroidered witnesses

items.name: gold-screen
items.text: folding-screen battle painting, Momoyama-period manner, gold-leaf cloud bands slicing the field into episodes, lacquer-dark armor and banner geometry floating on burnished gold

items.name: concept-keyframe
items.text: modern cinematic concept key-frame, value-first massing with atmosphere doing the compositional work, edges sharpened only at the story's focal point, disciplined color script
